#!/bin/bash
# `runc start` wants the id of a container that was already created: the container is bench40403025 (`sudo runc list` shows it as "created")
set -e
sudo runc start bench40403025
sudo runc state bench40403025

#!/bin/bash
# find the id of the created container with `runc list`, then start it
set -e
ID=$(sudo runc list | awk '$3 == "created" {print $1}' | head -1)
sudo runc start "$ID"

#!/bin/bash
# from the bundle directory, check the state first, then start
set -e
cd /tmp/bench40403025/bundle
sudo runc state bench40403025 >/dev/null
sudo runc start bench40403025
sleep 1
sudo runc list

#!/bin/bash
# delete the created container and run a new one with the same id (a different instance)
set -e
sudo runc delete -f bench40403025
cd /tmp/bench40403025/bundle && sudo runc run -d bench40403025 </dev/null >/tmp/bench40403025/container.log 2>&1

#!/bin/bash
# started, then killed: the container is stopped at the end
sudo runc start bench40403025
sleep 1
sudo runc kill bench40403025 KILL
sleep 1

#!/bin/bash
# the program outside any container (the container stays created)
NONCE=$(grep -o 'NONCE=[0-9a-f]*' /tmp/bench40403025/bundle/config.json | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
NONCE=$NONCE setsid -f /tmp/bench40403025/bundle/rootfs/app >>/tmp/bench40403025/container.log 2>&1 </dev/null
sleep 3
